title: Get-home planning: when the usual journey fails
review_status: Source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
tldr: Choose a safe waiting place, a backup way home and a check-in plan before your commute fails. Getting home is a decision, not an instruction to walk through danger.
steps: Identify where you depend on a bridge, transit line, lift, ferry or single road. List safe places you could wait near work, school and regular destinations.
Write down an alternate route, a pickup location and a place to stay if travel becomes unsafe. Confirm arrangements with the person who would help; an assumed ride is not a plan.
Keep comfortable shoes, weather protection, water, a small snack, a light, charging supplies and necessary personal items within realistic carrying limits.
Set an out-of-area contact, a time to check in and what the household should do if a message does not arrive. Use plain location descriptions and avoid broadcasting sensitive details.
sections: A route is more than a line on a map

Editorial route check: look for legal pedestrian access, lighting, terrain, shelter, water access and places where the route could be blocked. A road journey that takes twenty minutes can be a very different trip on foot. Do not assume an unfamiliar shortcut, rail corridor or highway shoulder is usable.
Decide whether to travel at all

Compare the conditions outside with the waiting place you already have. Weather, smoke, flooding, injury or unrest can make a journey worse than a delay. Discuss that tradeoff with your household in advance so an overdue arrival does not automatically trigger a second unsafe journey by someone looking for you.
without_help: If transit and communications fail, use the previously agreed waiting place or backup destination if accessible and safe. Reassess conditions rather than setting off simply because messages are not arriving.
household: Plan school pickup authority, care handover, mobility limits and pets left at home. Make sure your backup helper knows what they can realistically do and where their responsibility ends.
pack_now: Written addresses and contact numbers, walking shoes if needed, weather layer, light and a charged phone or compatible power bank.
next: Choose one regular journey and identify the first safe waiting place, one backup destination and a person who knows the plan.
watch: Do not cross floodwater or enter restricted routes to shorten a journey. Avoid meeting arrangements that force someone else to travel into the same hazard.
faqs: Is this the same as a bug-out bag?
No. This plan starts with a disrupted everyday journey. Keep the carry load small and matched to the distance and weather; evacuation planning covers leaving the home for a different destination.
scope: Civilian household planning. U.S. references; local services and rules differ. Planning examples are editorial suggestions, not promises of assistance.
